New Delhi, Nov 07: Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday launched the Semicon 2.0 web application portal under the Semicon India Programme and announced approval of 12 additional applications under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), involving projected investments of Rs 7,503 crore.
The initiatives aim to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem and expand domestic electronics component manufacturing capabilities.
The launch follows the Union Cabinet’s approval of Semicon 2.0 with a fiscal outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM).
The programme focuses on six strategic pillars covering chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication facilities, ATMP/OSAT units, research and development, and talent development.
Applications have now opened for Pillars 2, 3 and 4, covering semiconductor machinery and materials, new fabrication facilities, and the assembly, testing, marking and packaging ecosystem.

Highlighting the progress under the first phase, the government said 12 semiconductor projects involving investments exceeding Rs 1.64 lakh crore have been approved across six states, with five already commencing commercial production as of October 2026.
The ecosystem has also expanded through startup and academic participation.
As many as 105 startups have received access to Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, 24 startups have received funding support, and 15 have secured venture capital investments.
Additionally, 332 academic institutions have been provided EDA tools under the Chips to Startup programme, helping train approximately 70,000 students.
The latest 12 ECMS approvals are expected to generate production worth Rs 39,045 crore and create 7,127 direct jobs.
The projects cover multilayer printed circuit boards, relays, heat sinks, specialty ceramics, copper foil, anode material, cathode active material, polypropylene film and camera rims.
They will be established across Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.
The government highlighted that copper foil, cathode active material and specialty ceramics have received first-time support under ECMS.

Vaishnaw said India’s electronics manufacturing industry was moving beyond basic assembly towards developing capabilities in components, modules, materials and advanced technologies, creating opportunities for MSMEs.

The launch of Semicon 2.0 and the latest ECMS approvals mark another step in India’s efforts to build a comprehensive semiconductor and electronics manufacturing ecosystem, strengthen domestic supply chains, attract investments and generate employment.
